title: Why Reading/Watching Grappler Baki will make you JACKED
summary: NH's first manga recommendation, arguing for the original Grappler Baki (1991) over the later Netflix-adapted arcs. Every character is jacked, older characters stay muscular, the training and fights are extreme, the psychology runs deeper than it looks, and the story carries an anti-steroid message, all of which he says will motivate you to train.
claims: The original Grappler Baki (1991) is the best part of the saga; its first 42 volumes contain the plot elements needed to understand the later arcs, which Netflix adapted from 2018
Constant exposure to great physiques in Baki reminds you that you can and should strive for a better body
Baki's characters have very thick upper backs and necks and tree-trunk legs; size rarely equals strength in the power rankings
Baki shows men in their 50s still jacked, a good message that age is no barrier to building a physique
Jack Hanma is the only character in the story who uses steroids, out of impatience with his skinny body, and the author gives a strong anti-steroid message at the end of the second arc
Since your existence is shaped by what influences you, regularly exposing yourself to stories of alpha males fighting to be the strongest is a good decision
Seeing characters risk their lives to get stronger puts excuses like being tired or rain into perspective; skipping for those reasons is unacceptable
Baki covers serious themes like body dysmorphia, depression and the meaning of life that are relevant to a bodybuilding journey
